extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing NIDCD/NIH grant applications (including early-career investigators) seeking examples of successful R01 and R21 applications and summary statements
extracted.subtask_description: A resource page providing sample full applications and summary statements for NIDCD Research Project Grants (R01), Early Career Research (ECR) R21 awards, and Exploratory/Developmental R21 awards, plus brief guidance about mechanism scope, purpose, and usage restrictions. Useful for applicants preparing institute-specific NIH proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity’s specific instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that applicants must adhere to the specific instructions of the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA); sample applications illustrate successful approaches but do not replace FOA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on NIDCD scientific mission areas (ECR R21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The research must be focused on one or more of NIDCD's scientific mission areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ECR R21 applications will only be appropriate if the project aligns with NIDCD's mission; applicants should verify topical fit before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate project types for NIDCD ECR R21
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIDCD ECR Award R21 supports projects including secondary analysis of existing data; small, self-contained research projects; development of research methodology; translational research; outcomes research; and development of new research technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should structure proposals to fit one of these project types when applying to the ECR R21 mechanism; examples on the page illustrate these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of ECR R21: generate preliminary data for R01
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of the NIDCD ECR Award R21 is for the program director(s)/principal investigator(s) to obtain sufficient preliminary data for a subsequent R01 application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be designed to produce pilot/preliminary results that justify and enable a future R01 submission; this expectation guides project scope and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental) supports early/conceptual stage work
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Exploratory/Developmental R21 grant mechanism encourages exploratory and developmental research by providing support for the early and conceptual stages of project development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the R21 for high-risk/high-reward or proof-of-concept studies rather than fully mature R01-scale projects; aims and methods can reflect exploratory objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-standardized R21 application characteristics and review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has standardized the Exploratory/Developmental Grant (R21) application characteristics, requirements, preparation, and review procedures in order to accommodate investigator-initiated (unsolicited) grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult NIH/NIDCD guidance on standardized R21 requirements and review criteria when preparing submissions; samples illustrate past compliant formatting and content but applicants must follow current standardized rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 projects should be distinct from R01-funded projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be distinct from those supported through the traditional R01 mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a project is essentially the same as an R01-scale proposal, it is not appropriate for the R21; applicants should justify how the R21’s exploratory scope differs from an R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: R01 mechanism appropriate for investigator-led projects in PI's competence area
rubrics_metrics.description: R01 grants are awarded to organizations on behalf of an individual (a principal investigator, or PI) to facilitate pursuit of a research objective in the area of the investigator's research interests and competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose R01 projects that align with the PI's expertise and established research program; R01 is the traditional, larger-scale mechanism for mature research projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples demonstrate grantsmanship but may be outdated
rubrics_metrics.description: Although these samples demonstrate stellar grantsmanship, time has passed since these applications were submitted and the samples may not reflect changes in format or instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the samples as illustrative examples of strong applications, but always verify current NIH/NIDCD formatting, page limits, forms, and FOA-specific instructions before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of sample application text
rubrics_metrics.description: The application text is copyrighted. You may use it only for nonprofit educational purposes provided the document remains unchanged and the researcher, the grantee organization, and NIDCD are all credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reusing or distributing sample text, do not alter the document and include required credits; commercial or altered reuse is not permitted by the page notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 accessibility and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: These sample applications have been reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology; contact the NIDCD web team if you have trouble accessing the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants requiring accessible formats or experiencing access issues should reach out to the listed web team; samples have been adjusted for Section 508 compliance but may still pose accessibility problems for some users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sample summary statements and full applications as exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides full applications and corresponding summary statements from successful NIDCD investigators to benefit the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review both the full application and the summary statement together to understand reviewer critiques and how applicants responded; these paired documents are intended as teaching tools for crafting competitive proposals.
